sections.h2: The ₹25,000 ceiling is worth about ₹14,520 in 2014 rupees, less than the old ₹15,000

chart.title: Inflation cut the 2014 ceiling to ₹8,710; the new ₹25,000 is worth ₹14,520
chart.source: MoSPI consumer price index; post's own deflation.

sections.means: The ₹15,000 ceiling set in 2014 was worth about ₹8,710 by August 2026, and the new ₹25,000 only restores it to about ₹14,520 in 2014 money.
sections.todo: Index the ceiling to prices or wages so it moves without waiting for a new decision.

sections.h2: Since 2001 the ceiling has moved twice, after gaps of 13 and 12 years

chart.title: Gaps between ceiling changes reached 18 years in 1985 and 12 to 13 since 2001
chart.sub: Years from one ceiling change to the next.
chart.source: Business Today compilation; Nishith Desai Associates.

sections.means: Each long gap let the ceiling fall behind wages, and the ceiling has been held fixed for 12 to 18 years at a time.
sections.todo: Set a fixed review date for the ceiling so a gap of more than a decade cannot build up again.

sections.h2: Minimum wages in Delhi and Haryana already exceed the old ₹15,000 ceiling

chart.title: Delhi's and Haryana's unskilled minimum wages were above the old ₹15,000 ceiling
chart.source: Figures as cited in the post; ESI threshold per the post.

sections.means: The minimum wage in Delhi and Haryana already sat above the ₹15,000 ceiling, so workers there were outside compulsory cover.
sections.todo: Align the provident fund ceiling with the ESI threshold so the two schemes cover the same workers.

sections.h2: The employer's pension contribution rises 67% for members already above ₹15,000

chart.title: Employer pension share rises from ₹1,250 to about ₹2,083 a month on a ₹25,000 base
chart.sub: Employer's contribution to the pension scheme, ₹ a month.
chart.source: Standard statutory rates (8.33%), as worked out in the post.

sections.means: Contributions for members already earning above ₹15,000 are worked out on pay up to the new ceiling, so the statutory base rises from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000.
sections.todo: Publish the scheme's actuarial valuation so the larger pension promise can be checked.
